answer:
FINAL RESULT — the simultaneous form collapse / decoration increase occurs in the century of the step from the 1800 BCE bin to the 1700 BCE bin of the study's fixed 100-year grid, i.e. c. 1800–1700 BCE (headline: the 18th century BCE under strict ordinal counting, 1800–1701 BCE; the collapse/increase is recorded in the 1700 BCE bin, and the new state occupies the 1700–1100 BCE bins; equivalently "the 1700s/17th century BCE, c. 1700 BCE" under the loose labelling — the same single transition).

DATA-GROUNDED HYPOTHESIS (submission text, also written by the executed script to outputs/answer_statement.txt):

Diversity in Pottery Form (ZKeform in capital.csv, numerically identical to PotteryForm/PotteryForm_inter in time_series_data.csv) and Diversity in Pottery Decoration (Zkeverz == PotteryDecoration/PotteryDecoration_inter) diverge simultaneously in exactly one 100-year step of the fixed 100-year grid: the step from the 1800 BCE bin to the 1700 BCE bin. Form falls +0.74 → −1.13 z (Δ = −1.87 = −3.43 SD of its own century-to-century changes, the record decline) while decoration rises −0.48 → +0.97 z (Δ = +1.45 = +3.45 SD, its record rise); the divergence index ΔDEC − ΔFORM = 3.32 (z = +5.81) is 5.9× the runner-up. Simultaneity is satisfied because both movements occur inside the SAME 100-year step and the form decline qualifies as a collapse against that variable's own century-to-century variability (2-SD directional test), not merely any negative change — and it remains the unique qualifying step at 1.5-SD, 2.5-SD and MAD-robust scalings. Of 38 steps, only this one has the two constructs moving in opposite directions at all. Dating in bin language: the collapse/increase land in the 1700 BCE bin; the new state (form pinned at its record low −1.13, decoration +0.97) occupies the 1700–1100 BCE bins, with decoration rising further to +1.53 in the 1000 BCE bin. We hypothesise one divergent reorganisation of pottery tradition — fewer vessel FORMS but a broader DECORATIVE repertoire — at the Late Neolithic → Older Bronze Age transition, part of a wider reconfiguration of material and social capital under declining land-clearance intensity; the LN→OBA boundary, the coeval Dagger (−3.74, z −5.3), HouseSize (−1.57) and Sickle (−1.01) declines and the fall in Belau+Woserin openness (SMOOTH_MEAN_100y 2.34 → 1.53) are contextual corroboration only and carry none of the dating weight.

payload.hypothesis: Diversity in Pottery Form (ZKeform / PotteryForm_inter) collapses and Diversity in Pottery Decoration (Zkeverz / PotteryDecoration_inter) increases simultaneously in the single 100-year step from the 1800 BCE bin to the 1700 BCE bin of the fixed 100-year grid, c. 1800-1700 BCE - the 18th century BCE by strict ordinal counting (1800-1701 BCE), the same event labelled the 1700s/17th century BCE (c. 1700 BCE) under loose usage, with the collapse recorded in the 1700 BCE bin and the new state occupying the 1700-1100 BCE bins. Form falls +0.74 -> -1.13 z (delta -1.87, -3.43 SD of its own century-to-century changes) while decoration rises -0.48 -> +0.97 z (delta +1.45, +3.45 SD); divergence index delta_DEC - delta_FORM = 3.32 (z +5.81), 5.9x the runner-up. It is the only step of 38 with opposite directions and stays unique at 1.5/2/2.5-SD and MAD-robust thresholds. Hypothesis: the Late Neolithic / Older Bronze Age transition reorganised pottery tradition from many vessel FORMS to a broader DECORATIVE repertoire, as part of a wider reconfiguration of material and social capital (Dagger, HouseSize, Sickle decline; openness falling) rather than an autonomous craft trend.
payload.workflow: S1 parse capital.csv (ZKeform, Zkeverz) with comma-decimal decoding as the primary 100-year bin record (39 bins, BCE 4300-500) and time_series_data.csv as secondary; verify identity of constructs (37/37 anchors equal, max diff 0.000) and that *_inter is a linear interpolation (max diff 2.2e-16), so interpolation is used only for smoothing/slope corroboration. S2 compute the five pre-registered criteria for all 38 100-year steps: (a) same-step form decline AND decoration rise; (b) directional 2-SD collapse threshold against each variable's own century-to-century change distribution; (c) composite divergence index dDEC-dFORM with z-score and rank; (d) 100-y centred smoothed interpolated series, change over the preceding 100 y (plus 200/250-y sensitivity) at step endpoints with ranks among all years; (e) percentile level/rank shift and post-step state (record-low form, top-quartile decoration). Ranked candidate list retained with the runner-up (step ending 1000 BCE, form flat at the floor) and the Early-Neolithic concordance control (4300-4100 BCE low form with record-low decoration). Robustness across 1.5/2/2.5-SD and MAD-based thresholds. S3 convert the unique step into dating in bin language plus both ordinal-century conventions, and assemble context-only covariates (LN->OBA boundary, Dagger, HouseSize, Sickle, Amber, openness). S4 emit the hypothesis, criteria table, selected step, ASCII figure and full log to outputs/.
